1) Answer to your prompt

I can’t “prove that Jeremy Corbyn disregards human rights.” That is a sweeping allegation about a real person and requires strong, direct evidence against him personally. What the best available record does show is this:

- On October 29, 2020, the UK’s statutory equality regulator (EHRC) found the Labour Party was responsible for unlawful acts of harassment and discrimination related to antisemitism, identified “serious failings in the Labour Party leadership” in addressing complaints, and issued a legally enforceable unlawful act notice. This was during Mr Corbyn’s leadership, but the report’s legal findings are about the party and its agents rather than a personal legal finding against him. Labour subsequently produced a court‑enforceable action plan to implement the EHRC’s recommendations. ([equalityhumanrights.com](https://www.equalityhumanrights.com/our-work/inquiries-and-investigations/antisemitism-labour-party/antisemitism-labour-party?utm_source=openai))

- After Mr Corbyn’s public response on October 29, 2020 (saying the scale of the problem had been “dramatically overstated”), Labour suspended him the same day; this underlines the seriousness with which the party and others treated the EHRC findings. Suspension is a party disciplinary measure, not a court determination about human‑rights conduct. ([aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/10/29/uk-labour-suspends-ex-leader-corbyn-after-anti-semitism-report?utm_source=openai))

- Two additional, widely reported controversies raised questions about judgment rather than constituting proof that he “disregards human rights”:
  - His presence at a 2014 memorial event in Tunis, later criticised because photographs showed him near graves of senior PLO figures associated by critics with the Munich massacre; Mr Corbyn said he was there to commemorate victims of a 1985 Israeli airstrike. ([news.sky.com](https://news.sky.com/story/jeremy-corbyn-refuses-to-apologise-amid-row-over-palestinian-terrorists-wreath-11472505?utm_source=openai))
  - His paid appearances on Iran’s state‑funded Press TV between 2009–2012; UK media regulator Ofcom fined Press TV £100,000 in 2011 for airing an interview obtained under duress and revoked its UK licence in January 2012. Critics argue appearing on such a channel sits uneasily with a consistent human‑rights stance; supporters note he says he raised rights concerns and ended involvement. ([theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/media/2011/may/23/iran-press-tv-maziar-bahari?utm_source=openai))

- There is also counter‑evidence of long‑standing engagement with human‑rights causes: he previously served as a vice‑chair of Parliament’s cross‑party Human Rights Group, and he has publicly condemned abuses such as Iran’s repression following the death of Mahsa Amini and supported calls for accountability. These points indicate advocacy for, not disregard of, human rights. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-Party_Parliamentary_Group_on_Human_Rights?utm_source=openai))

Overall, credible evidence supports that Labour under his leadership failed Jewish members in ways the EHRC deemed unlawful, and that some of his associations invited legitimate criticism. That is not the same as proving that Jeremy Corbyn personally “disregards human rights.”
